defects.description: Every response now confirms the misconception that the filter understands messages.
No-device path reduced to 'read the lesson aloud'.
Every segment's instructions reduced to 'Run this part' / 'Follow along'.

objectivesPlain: A junk filter gives points for clues, adds them into a score, and sends a message to junk if the score reaches a line called the threshold.
A filter only counts clues. It does not understand the message, so it can be fooled, and a real message can land in junk.
before: Open the lesson in classroom mode on the projector. Page Down or a clicker moves one step.
On the board, draw columns Junk and Inbox, and write the rule: 1 point per "!", 2 per money word (won, prize, free, pay, fee), 3 per urgent word (urgent, now, only today).

artifact.ifYouDontKnow: It is fine not to know. Say: "Good question. I do not know. Let us find out together." Then return to what this filter does: it counts clues against a line.
artifact.parentNote: Today your child built a tiny junk filter: it gives points for clues, adds them up, and blocks a message if the total reaches a line. Ask: "How would you fool it? Why can a happy message from a friend end up in junk?" Lessons on this platform are made with AI assistance and reviewed by the creator.
